newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BAGGIO JOINS BOLOGNA WITH WORLD CUP IN MIND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAGGIO JOINS BOLOGNA WITH WORLD CUP IN MIND.

text.p: Roberto Baggio joined Bologna from AC Milan on Friday and vowed to prove his critics wrong by reclaiming his place in the Italian national team for next year's World Cup in France.
Baggio signed a two-year deal with Bologna, who just missed out on a UEFA Cup place last season, ending weeks of speculation during which he had been linked to clubs in Italy, Spain and England.
"I've chosen Bologna, a choice which makes me very happy," he told a news conference in Milan. "From Sunday I'll be at the coach's service.

"To find a team like Bologna in the year before a World Cup is great," he said. "Everything is at stake for me and I hope to make it to France. I want to prove that the people who have written me off are wrong."
Bologna president Giuseppe Gazzoni Frascara, who was also at the conference, said Baggio would be free to leave after one season if he so wished.
"He has a lot of freedom," said Gazzoni Frascara, who declined to give details of the transfer fee, reported by Italian newspapers to be around $3 million.
Baggio, 30, said last month he was leaving Milan after a frustrating season in which he was often sidelined with sciatica and constantly left on the substitutes' bench even when he was fit.

Milan coach Fabio Capello had hinted there was no place for "The Divine Ponytail" in his plans for next season and the club said they were open to offers for one of the most influential Italian players of his generation.

The attacking midfielder was linked to several clubs including Vicenza -- where he made his professional debut 15 years ago -- Parma, Udinese, England's Derby County, Spain's Barcelona and Atletico Madrid and finally Bologna.
Milan said earlier this week they were happy with the fee Bologna had offered and were waiting to hear from Baggio if he was satisfied with the personal terms on offer.
Italian media said Baggio would earn around $1.6 million-a-year at Bologna, slightly less than his salary at Milan.
Baggio said he was sorry to leave Milan, where he has spent the last two seasons.
"Milan are a great side," he said. "I would like to have given them more but I didn't have the opportunities to play much for them."
Baggio, capped 46 times, has said he dearly wants to play in the 1998 World Cup and was keen to ensure himself first team football next season so he could prove himself to Italy coach Cesare Maldini.
Baggio was a national hero in the last World Cup, scoring inspired last-minute goals against Nigeria and Spain to help propel Italy into the final.
But he also missed a penalty with the last kick of the championship, handing the trophy to Brazil.
